start.name: Baltim South West offshore production platform (Nile Delta, ~12 km off the Baltim/Mediterranean coast, 23–25 m water depth)
start.coord_basis: Baltim village (coastal town, Kafr El Sheikh) is at 31.5544N/31.0903E per OpenStreetMap node 768568179. Eni's own press release, NS Energy Business, and Offshore Magazine all independently describe the Baltim South West platform as ~12 km off the Baltim/Mediterranean coast (NS Energy: platform in 23 m water, field in 25 m water). Offsetting Baltim's coordinate 12 km due north (12/111.32=0.108 deg lat) gives 31.5544+0.108=31.662N, 31.090E. This is a geometric approximation (due-north offset from a coastal town), NOT a surveyed platform coordinate — no source publishes exact platform lat/lon.

end.name: Baltim coast landfall (Baltim, Kafr El Sheikh) — tie-in to onshore leg P7578
end.coord_basis: Baltim village/town centroid per OpenStreetMap node 768568179 (31.5544N, 31.0903E). No source explicitly states the exact landfall point; inferred from the field being named 'Baltim South West' and three independent sources (Eni, NS Energy, Offshore Magazine) placing the platform ~12 km off 'the Baltim coast.' Treated as the same point as P7578's start (subsea line ends where the onshore line begins).

notes: Sheet length 18.0 km for the 'Sub-Sea Pipeline' segment is independently corroborated: Daily News Egypt (2019-08-27, quoting Petrobel) states Petrobel built an '18 km-long, 26-inch-diameter offshore production line and 25 km-long, 26-inch-diameter onshore line' for Baltim South West — matching the 18.0/25.0 km sheet split exactly. This is a second independent source beyond the prior pass's sfegypt.com citation, both giving identical numbers. Platform location is confirmed by 3 sources to be ~12 km off the Baltim coast in 23-25 m water, on the Baltim South development lease (Eni/bp 50/50, operated by Petrobel on behalf of Medgas); however no source gives a surveyed platform lat/lon, so the start point remains a geometric approximation flagged as such. Landfall-at-Baltim is inferred (reasonable, but not an explicit statement in any source found) from the field's naming and the consistent 'off the Baltim coast' framing. end.name: Abu Madi Gas Plant (onshore gas treatment plant), Nile Delta, Egypt
end.coord_basis: WEAKEST-CONFIDENCE point of the batch. No source found gives a surveyed lat/lon for the Abu Madi Gas Plant itself, and an OpenStreetMap Overpass search for a tagged 'Abu Madi' facility timed out / returned nothing usable (Nominatim also returns no match — only unrelated 'Abu Madi' place names in Matrouh, Cairo and Alexandria). Derived by projecting the sheet's 25.0 km onshore-line length due south from the Baltim landfall (31.5544N, 31.0903E): 25/111.32 deg = 0.2246 deg lat, so 31.5544-0.2246=31.330N, longitude held constant (no bearing evidence found, so due-south is the most conservative placement — treat as a rough placeholder). GlobalData's field profile places the 'Abu Madi Development Lease Field' administratively in Dakahlia governorate (east/southeast of this point), which would argue for a coordinate further east; this discrepancy is unresolved (an academic source giving an 'Abu Madi-1 well' coordinate at 31.438N/31.354E could not be used — its host returned HTTP 403 on url_verifier.py and no second accessible source corroborated it). RECOMMEND GIS/imagery confirmation of this specific endpoint before finalizing route geometry.

notes: Sheet length 25.0 km for the 'Onshore Pipeline' segment matches Daily News Egypt's reported '25 km-long, 26-inch-diameter onshore line' exactly (second independent source beyond the prior pass's sfegypt.com citation). The Abu Madi Gas Plant as the pipeline's terminus is very well corroborated (Eni official release, NS Energy, Offshore Magazine, Daily News Egypt, and a separate DMS Universe project page on the adjoining 'Nooros-Abu Madi-El Gamil' pipeline all name it as the receiving/treatment plant, with gas onward-piped to El Gamil near Port Said and into the national grid) — so resolved:true reflects strong confidence in WHICH facility this is, not in its exact coordinate (see end.coord_basis — flagged for human GIS check). Independently attempted to improve the Abu Madi coordinate myself (OSM Nominatim, Overpass API, Wikipedia) after the subagent flagged it weak; no better public source found. All 4 route_refs URLs re-verified via url_verifier.py (200 OK).

start.name: Cronos gas field wellhead/manifold, Cyprus Block 6 (Eni-operated, Eni/TotalEnergies 50/50), Cyprus EEZ
start.coord_basis: No official surveyed coordinate for Cronos was found in any public source (Eni/TotalEnergies press releases, Cyprus CHC licensed-blocks page, Wikidata all omit it). Triangulated approximation combining two independently reported distances: ~70 km from the Zohr field (en.protothema.gr) and ~160-185 km SW of Cyprus's coast (offshore-mag.com: 185 km; discoveryalert.com.au / drillingcontractor.org: 160 km; maritime-executive.com: '90 nm' ≈ 167 km), anchored on Zohr's coordinate (33°00'N, 32°30'E, Wikidata). Cross-checked for plausibility against the neighboring Aphrodite/Block 12 field (33°05'40"N, 32°59'0"E). Treat as approximate (±~20-30 km) — adequate for a great-circle corridor, not survey-grade.

end.name: Zohr field subsea/offshore infrastructure tie-in point, Shorouk Block, Egypt EEZ (NOT Port Said itself)
end.coord_basis: Zohr field-center coordinate (33°00'N, 32°30'E) per Wikidata (Q20894861). Cross-checked by arithmetic from the stated '190 km north of Port Said, Shorouk Block' description: Port Said (~31.27N, 32.30E) + 190 km due north lands at ~32.98N, consistent with the Wikidata point.

sheet_conflicts: The sheet name 'Cronos-Port Said Gas Pipeline' is misleading and does not match what's actually being built. Per the FID announcement (28 July 2026, Eni/TotalEnergies), this is a trans-boundary subsea tieback connecting the Cronos wellhead directly to EXISTING ZOHR FIELD INFRASTRUCTURE (~70 km away) — it does NOT run to Port Said or make landfall at all. From Zohr, gas is processed at Zohr's existing offshore facilities, then separately piped onward via Zohr's own pre-existing ~218 km trunk line to the Damietta LNG terminal for liquefaction (not Port Said/El Gamil). 'Port Said' only appears in sourcing as a distance reference for Zohr's location ('190 km north of Port Said'), never as an actual pipeline terminus. The sheet's 90.0 km length corroborates this: it's the right order of magnitude for the short Cronos-Zohr subsea tieback (~70-90 km depending on source), and far too short for any direct run to Port Said or Damietta (which would be 250-300+ km). Recommend the tracker's endpoint/name be corrected from 'Port Said' to 'Zohr field infrastructure' or similar (Baird's call — flagged here, not applied).
notes: Cronos is an Eni-operated (50%) / TotalEnergies (50%) gas discovery (2022, appraised 2024) in Cyprus Block 6, ~3.1 tcf gas in place, FID taken 28 July 2026 with first gas targeted 2028 (~500 MMcf/d plateau). Developed via four subsea wells tied back across the Cyprus-Egypt EEZ boundary to existing Zohr field facilities (Shorouk Block, Egypt), then onward through Zohr's existing infrastructure to Damietta LNG for export as LNG to Europe. Both endpoints corroborated by multiple independent outlets (Offshore Magazine, Maritime Executive, ProtoThema, Drilling Contractor, Offshore Technology) reporting consistent distance figures, but the Cronos endpoint lacks a published survey coordinate, so its lon/lat here is a distance-triangulated approximation — good enough for an indicative corridor, not a precise route. start.name: Qattameya gas field (subsea wellhead), North Damietta offshore concession
start.coord_basis: Arithmetic: 60 km due north of Damietta city (31.4165N, 31.8133E, a standard geographic reference point) per offshore-technology.com and pipeline-journal.net descriptions of the Qattameya field location (North Damietta offshore concession, 108m water depth). Cross-checked via the independently reported Atoll-1 well position (32.2236N, 31.9062E) and the stated Atoll-Salamat (15km) and Qattameya-Salamat (30km SW) offsets, which triangulate to within ~15km of this point — inside the fuzziness of the source language.

end.name: Ha'py platform, Ras El Bar concession
end.coord_basis: Arithmetic: 45 km due east of the Qattameya start point, per the repeatedly stated 'Qattameya field located approximately 45km west of the Ha'py platform' (offshore-technology.com; pipeline-journal.net). Ha'py is the fixed platform in the Ha'py/Tuart subsea system — Tuart is itself subsea-only and tied back to Ha'py via a separate ~70km line (egyptoil-gas.com) — so Ha'py is the physical tie-in point of this specific 50km Qattameya pipeline. The 45km straight-line distance vs. the sheet's 50.0km pipeline length is consistent with normal route slack.

sheet_conflicts: None material. StartLocation 'North Damietta offshore concession' and EndLocation 'Hapy&Tuart Gas Field facilities' at 50.0km both check out against independent industry reporting of this exact tie-back pipeline. One nuance: 'Hapy&Tuart' names the combined downstream gas stream/processing hub, but the physical tie-in point of THIS 50km line is the Ha'py platform specifically (Tuart is a subsea-only development linked to Ha'py by its own separate ~70km pipeline) — so the endpoint modeled here is Ha'py, not a blended Ha'py/Tuart location.
notes: Operator is bp (concession operator, 50%), with Eni's Egyptian affiliate IEOC holding the other 50% in the Ras El Bar/North Damietta concessions. Sheet's 'Tuart' spelling matches pipeline-journal.net verbatim (offshore-technology.com instead uses 'Taurt' — both spellings attested in industry sources, so no correction proposed). No public source gives raw coordinates for either point; both derived via stated distances/bearings from well-known reference points rather than invented or read off a map. start.name: Wanda gas well (Khalda Petroleum exploration well, Egypt Western Desert — specific concession/block not publicly named)
start.coord_basis: No coordinates or concession/block name published in any source found; location given only as 'Western Desert, Egypt.'

end.name: Unnamed existing Khalda Petroleum production/gathering infrastructure, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Sources state the new pipeline links the well to 'existing infrastructure' but never name the receiving facility, field, or gathering station.

sheet_conflicts: The task brief hypothesized an offshore Nile Delta/Mediterranean tieback for Wanda; that hypothesis is NOT supported. All corroborating reporting (Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum, TradeArabia, Zawya, EgyptToday, ArabFinance, and multiple Arabic outlets, all tracing to the same 22 July 2026 Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources announcement) places Wanda ONSHORE in Egypt's Western Desert, operated by Khalda Petroleum (an EGPC/APA Corporation 50/50 JV) — not offshore, not Nile Delta. If the sheet's country/location metadata for P7605 says offshore Mediterranean/Nile Delta, that metadata itself needs review (Baird's call).
notes: Found the project: Wanda is a deep gas exploration well (15,000 ft) in Egypt's Western Desert, operated by Khalda Petroleum (50/50 EGPC/APA Corporation JV). Ministry of Petroleum announced (22 July 2026) it began production at 40 mmcf/d, and that Khalda built a new 10-km production pipeline ($2.3M) linking the well to 'existing infrastructure' to fast-track output ahead of national-grid tie-in expected end of July 2026. The reported 10 km pipeline length matches the sheet's stated 10.0 km exactly, strongly confirming this is the right project despite the wrong offshore/Nile-Delta assumption in the task brief. However, every source found (a dozen+ outlets, all derivative of one Ministry press release, checked in English and Arabic) is silent on: (1) which of Khalda's many Western Desert concessions/blocks (e.g. Qarun, Matruh, Shushan, Faghur Basin, Salam, Obaiyed areas) Wanda sits in, (2) the name of the 'existing infrastructure'/facility the new line ties into, (3) any coordinates, and (4) nearby named fields. This is a brand-new discovery (announced ~1 week before this research) with no field development plan, EGAS/EGPC bulletin, or map yet public. Some Arabic outlets (elaosboa.com, egcoop.com) transliterate the well name as 'Watda' (واتدا) — possible alternate spelling of the same well; not enough independent confirmation to recommend renaming the GEM entity. Recommend resolved:false with a corridor note ('somewhere in Khalda's Western Desert concession area, onshore Egypt') rather than fabricated coordinates — revisit once an EGAS annual report or more detailed trade-press follow-up names the specific concession.
